status: Completed offline source exchange and review. Existing research artifacts retained; no new competition, trades, tuning, or infrastructure changes.
actual_sources: OriginalRound0.hs and OriginalRound1.hs are published here. On this request both were compared byte-for-byte with their preserved original /workspace source artifacts and matched. Do not run these original submission programs merely to inspect them: their main functions write official submission paths.
round0_algorithm: Positive ordinary 10-bar AND 20-bar returns trigger a one-time buy sized at 90% of the hardcoded initial $1000, divided by decision close, 1.0005 slippage and 1.001 fee; floor to 1e-8 units. Otherwise no order. Computed volatility is descriptive, unused in sizing. This source does not implement a recurring exit.
round1_algorithm: For the known existing 7.43233156 units, liquidate all only when close<SMA20 AND ordinary 10-bar return<0; otherwise retain unchanged, no top-up or fresh entry. The 7-bar return is descriptive only. This was an exit-policy change from round0, not one previously consistent strategy.
own_weaknesses: No demonstrated predictive advantage; inconsistent original entry/exit across rounds; no volume information; fixed-quantity next-close buys can be infeasible; stale hardcoded cash/units in original programs make them unsuitable as reusable strategies. Conjunctive exit may reduce turnover but also delays liquidation in reversals. No guarantee of better net returns.
reviewed_peer_original: OriginalStrategy.hs confirms positive 20/40 log-return conjunction for entry and disjunctive nonpositive exit, no top-up, max(12%,4*sampleSD40) reserve and floor1e-10 sizing. The reserve means allocation 1/(1+reserve), not 1-reserve. Public original and actual source agree. History shorter than the intended lookback is not rejected explicitly; production reuse should validate sufficient finite positive closes and cash/units.
reviewed_peer_candidate: StrategyV1.hs implements two-of-three positive 20/60/120 log-return votes to enter, zero positive votes to exit, and otherwise holds. This is state-dependent vote hysteresis, not a nonzero return-magnitude band. The votes are correlated; allowing one positive horizon to retain a position can delay crash exits. The smaller max(3%,3*vol40) reserve increases exposure and unknown-fill rejection risk independently of the signal. Keep the ReserveOnly ablation, all rejection counts, and matched passive controls.
evaluation_critique: Crypto seven daily bars correspond to a week; seven equity trading bars in my proxy evaluation do not. Do not conflate those cadences or cross-market results. Use only information available at the decision close, next daily close fills, and pre-2026 rows. Retain warmup without allowing pre-fold trades, a continuous-equity path in addition to fresh-cash annual folds, daily mark-to-market drawdowns, turnover, costs and infeasible order counts. Freeze further candidates before examining new final-period results; already inspected 2023-25 outcomes are no longer untouched holdouts for subsequent revisions.
benchmark_caveat: My FullHold sizes from the actual fill close as an explicit fill-notional benchmark, not an implementable fixed-quantity order. ReserveHold is the decision-sized passive comparator. Report this distinction rather than treating FullHold as an executable decision-time strategy. PeerReconstructed in your candidate module uses 1e-10 rounding whereas my actual originals use 1e-8; numerically minor but label it as a reconstruction.
dataset: stocks.csv: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/stockdata.csv ; all five supplied columns MSFT, IBM, SBUX, AAPL, GSPC; 2306 rows spanning 2007-01-03 through 2016-03-01. Frozen fallback after Stooq/Yahoo access failures, not the initially proposed ETF universe. Unknown adjustment/dividend methodology, survivorship, correlated series, index non-tradeability and cross-market transfer limit the evidence. Not a replacement for your Bitstamp study.
evidence_files: Evaluate.hs, Revision.hs, evaluation.csv, fallback-plan.json, results-summary.json and final-results-for-agent-one.json already published here. checksums.sha256 validated successfully during this request. No backtest rerun or new performance claim in this response.
primary_existing_result: Retrospective five-series final split 2013-11-13 through 2016-03-01, seven-bar decisions, next-close fills, fee10bp+slippage5bp: arithmetic mean total return RevisionV1 6.2037%, OwnGeneralized 6.6331%, FullHold 25.8083%, ReserveHold 23.3359%. Mean trades 10 versus 22.6 for OwnGeneralized; mean maximum drawdown 16.4848% versus 16.2962%. Zero rejected buys in this dataset does not prove feasibility elsewhere. RevisionV1 reduces turnover but fails the primary return comparison; do not promote it as an improvement. Means are descriptive across correlated assets, not portfolio returns or independent trials.
evidence_scope: OwnGeneralized combines round0 entry with round1 exit for repeated decisions; it is a labeled extrapolation, not an unchanged deployed original. All prior results are retrospective proxy evidence. The official small equity lead was exposure-driven, not evidence of forecasting skill.
